rationale:
All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to abdominal aortic aneurysm), so a direct-match outcome is warranted. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA publication (Million Veteran Program AAA genetics paper) and reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which is a PRS-comparable signal absent from most other candidates here; its covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs), supporting comparability. The main limitation is that it is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2, while several genome-wide PRS-CS/LDpred2 models exist.

Runners-up: PGS003973 and PGS003972 are from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) using PRS-CS with ~1.1M variants and EUR evaluation; they provide full-model discrimination metrics (C-index 0.882 for PGS003973; AUROC 0.69 for PGS003972), but these are not explicitly PRS-only and covariates are unknown for PGS003972, reducing comparability. PGS001784 and PGS002054 are deprioritized as framework/portability-style scores despite having PRS-comparable R2/partial-r (~0.014–0.015), and PGS003429 is a screening cost-effectiveness context with only full-model AUROC and unknown covariates, making its performance less directly interpretable for standalone PRS selection. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (alcohol dependence) via trait_efo/phenotyping_reported mapping to alcohol dependence/alcohol use disorder. PGS002738 is best supported because it has the most endpoint-faithful labeling (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both alcohol use disorder; trait_efo alcohol dependence), a disease-focused multi-cohort development context (MVP, UKB), and the strongest visible discriminative evidence via effect size (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) on a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=7,900). Runners-up: PGS002739 is also endpoint-faithful and reports a strong OR top 10% vs rest (1.76, 95% CI 1.32–2.34) but is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples (AFR 100%), making it less directly comparable/portable if deployment ancestry is unspecified. Between the two ‘Problematic alcohol use’ siblings (PGS000201/PGS000202), both still use an AUD DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype, but their reported incremental ΔR² values are small (0.01192 and 0.00456) and effect sizes are weaker; PGS000201 is preferred over PGS000202 due to larger validation (n=7,599 vs 1,251) and stronger reported ΔR² and β. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because none of the candidates report clear PRS-only AUC/R², covariates are unknown for the top-ranked AUD models, and the remaining performance evidence is limited to incremental ΔR² or top-decile ORs, leaving residual uncertainty in cross-study comparability.

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis) with broadly aligned reported/phenotyped endpoints. PGS004913 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported exactly alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis) and appears disease-focused (heavy drinkers; dedicated cirrhosis PRS paper) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Its reported PRS-comparable metric is limited to an R²=0.029 (no AUROC provided), but it also reports a sizable decile contrast OR=4.4, supporting non-trivial discrimination.

PGS000704 is a strong runner-up due to very large UKB development/validation and a genome-wide model (183,271 variants; snpnet multi-PRS) with basic covariates; however, the only visible discrimination is a full-model C-index=0.711 and HR=1.18 per SD (moderate/weak), and the publication context is a broad biomarker genetics paper rather than a cirrhosis-focused PRS study, making PRS-only performance less clear.

PGS001777 ranks third: it is disease-focused and reports strong stratification (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18) but is extremely sparse (3 variants), has unknown covariates, and has a small validation sample (n=1,390), limiting confidence in robustness. Overall confidence is Moderate (not High) because none of the candidates reports clearly PRS-only AUROC, and the available metrics are not directly comparable across studies (full-model AUC/C-index vs R² vs stratified OR).

All 19 candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping_reported variants include Angina, ICD10 I20, and PheCode 411.3). Among models with PRS-comparable metrics, the snpnet UKB framework family (PGS001260/61/62) reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (~0.58) and PGS-only R2 (~0.012–0.013), which are interpretable and below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs ~0.009–0.014; liability h2 ~0.134), and uses only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). Within that family, PGS001262 has the strongest selected European full-model AUROC (0.807) and the highest incremental AUROC (0.0098) and PGS-only R2 (0.01304) among its siblings, while maintaining tight endpoint alignment (doctor-diagnosed angina). Runner-up PGS001261 is very similar but slightly weaker on the same reported PRS-only metrics (PGS-only R2 0.01228; incremental AUROC 0.00796). As a second runner-up, PGS005048 (MVP; PheCode 411.3) provides supportive effect-size evidence (OR 1.487) and a strong full-model C-index (0.7669) with basic covariates, but lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 and has N/A training sample metadata, limiting comparability. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the best-supported option comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (a known generalization risk per provided domain guidance) and several newer ICD10/PheCode models report only full-model metrics or ORs without PRS-only discrimination, preventing a clearly high-confidence single winner. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported align to ankylosing spondylitis), so a direct-match exists. For best_model_id, PGS002089 is preferred because it is a genome-wide shrinkage-style score (LDpred2; 22,026 variants) from the UKB portability study and reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0919 with CI) in European evaluation; within this same publication family it also has stronger partial-r than the penalized-regression sibling PGS001876 (partial-r 0.0797). As runners-up, PGS001267 and PGS001268 (snpnet sparse 10-variant models from the UKB ‘813 traits’ framework) are the only candidates in the list that report explicit PRS-only AUROC and PRS-only R² (and full-model AUROC with basic covariates), with PGS001268 slightly higher full-model AUROC/R² than PGS001267 but also using a time-to-event phenotype label; both are penalized by being pan-trait sparse framework scores. The Taiwanese EAS-only models (PGS003420–PGS003424) report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation size (n=1,298), making their performance less comparable to PRS-only metrics and limiting confidence. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because the evidence is conflicted/incomplete across families (partial-r vs PRS-only AUROC/R² vs full-model-only AUROC; differing study archetypes and ancestry contexts), so no single candidate is unequivocally best-supported. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254, PGS005255, PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it has exact trait alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo aortic stenosis) with endpoint-faithful phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases) and provides the richest comparable performance evidence in this list (reported C-index 0.87 plus HR=1.92) with large EUR evaluation (n=446,895). The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (e.g., T2D, HTN, CAD, lipids, BMI, smoking, renal failure), so it may be substantially covariate-driven and is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance.

Runners-up: PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis score with incident endpoint and a clear per-SD effect size (HR=1.64, with CI) and cleaner/basic covariates (age/sex/PCs), but it lacks reported AUC/R2/C-index and has smaller validation (n=244,450). Between the remaining direct-match set, PGS005255 (mean pressure gradient; trait_efo includes aortic stenosis/aortic measurement) is kept ahead of PGS005256 because both share the same endpoint/covariates/validation size and similar HR (~1.53), making them effectively tied; selecting one as the second runner-up is therefore low-resolution based on visible metadata. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including an exact-label model (PGS001135; trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported="Arthritis (nos)") and two additional arthritis-labeled models (PGS004477 and PGS004547; both trait_efo=arthritis; phenotyping_reported="M13 (Other arthritis)"). PGS001135 is the best-supported direct match because it is explicitly an arthritis (NOS) endpoint and reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.53928; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00291) plus full-model AUROC=0.67424, enabling at least some isolation of PRS contribution (and these PRS-only metrics are well below the provided arthritis heritability ceiling, consistent with the domain sanity-check guidance). However, overall evidence remains limited/weak for a clearly strong recommendation because the PRS-only discrimination is modest and the other arthritis candidates (PGS004477/PGS004547) provide only an OR without PRS-only AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates, making cross-model performance comparability poor. Runners-up are PGS004547 (OR=1.262198) and PGS004477 (OR=1.1956), both direct arthritis endpoints but with less comparable performance reporting than PGS001135. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are abundant (all map to asthma via trait_efo/trait_reported), so the task is to pick the best-supported asthma PRS based on endpoint fidelity, PRS-comparable performance evidence, and study archetype/covariates. PGS002727 is preferred because it is explicitly a disease-focused pediatric asthma PRS (phenotyping_reported: Pediatric asthma) with strong PRS signal via effect size (OR=1.57 per SD, CI 1.55–1.60) and a reported full-model AUROC=0.66 with R²=0.04, and it is developed in a multi-ancestry context (GWAS multi-ancestry; EVAL multi-ancestry) with very large validation support (n=391,820). The main limitation is that covariates are listed as Unknown and the AUROC is full-model (no explicit PGS-only AUROC), so comparability of the AUROC across candidates is imperfect.

Runner-up PGS001344 is a strong direct asthma endpoint (doctor-diagnosed asthma) with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates=0.64568; PGS R² no covariates=0.05973) and basic covariates, but it comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models in external validation; this keeps it behind PGS002727 despite clean metrics. Runner-up PGS001782 is a genome-wide shrinkage PRS-CS-auto score from a broad multi-biobank study (Cell Genom) with covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R²=0.048844 and full-model AUROC=0.659, offering a strong, methodologically modern alternative; it ranks behind PGS002727 mainly because it appears more framework/benchmarking-oriented and provides less direct effect-size evidence than the pediatric asthma PRS.

All 6 candidates are direct matches at the EFO level (atopic eczema) but differ materially in endpoint fidelity. PGS002755 is best supported because its phenotyping is a generic, target-aligned endpoint (“Incident atopic dermatitis”), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), and reports a PRS effect size (HR high vs low PRS 1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a large European evaluation (n=337,910), with only standard demographic/SES-style covariates listed. Runners-up: PGS004587 has the same incident atopic dermatitis endpoint and similarly large European evaluation with an HR (1.153, 95% CI 1.037–1.282), but is structurally weaker (23 genome-wide significant SNPs) and appears embedded in an exposure-focused study context (air pollution), making it less compelling as a standalone PRS. PGS001773 targets a narrower subtype (“Moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis”) and reports very high full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49), but these are full-model metrics (not PRS-only) and are likely not comparable; additionally the endpoint is severity-restricted and the variant set is very small (25), lowering confidence for generic atopic eczema risk. The remaining candidates (PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903) are primarily about paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (therapy-/context-specific phenotype), which is a weaker match to generic atopic eczema despite sharing the EFO mapping.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter), so selection is driven by endpoint fidelity plus the strongest, most comparable performance evidence without heavy risk-wrapper packaging. PGS005168 is best supported because it is a disease-focused AF meta-analysis PRS (Nat Genet 2025; PRS-CS; 382,963 variants) with a direct AF endpoint and strong reported discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) and effect-size evidence (HR 1.6663; beta reported), with basic covariates plus CHARGE-AF adjustment (noted as a potential packaging/clinical-calculator concern but still within a disease-focused AF study context). Runner-up PGS005313 is also disease-focused and reports strong AUROC (0.78 with tight CI) and OR (1.82) with basic covariates (age, sex), but has only a single visible performance record here and evaluation appears MAE-only, making its support slightly less broad/established than PGS005168’s multi-record evidence. Second runner-up PGS002814 is strongly supported for East Asian deployment (Nat Genet 2023; very large GWAS; AUROC 0.74; pseudo-R2 0.14; OR ~1.94) but is less general for an unspecified target population because its evaluation is EAS-only. Confidence is Moderate because several other direct-match candidates exist with high full-model metrics, but many lack PRS-comparable metrics or have endpoint packaging (e.g., 5-year risk predictors) that reduces comparability, and cross-study metric comparability (C-index vs AUROC; covariate sets) remains imperfect. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (atrial flutter) via trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported, but 3/4 are for the combined endpoint “atrial fibrillation and flutter,” reducing endpoint specificity for flutter alone. PGS001263 is the only exact atrial flutter model (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Atrial flutter”), and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.61716; PGS-only R2=0.02517) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Its PRS-only R2 is below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so nothing is obviously inconsistent. However, it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk; this prevents a high-quality designation despite the exact phenotype match and available PRS-only metrics.

Runner-up PGS001339 remains a direct match because the endpoint explicitly includes atrial flutter, and it provides similar PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.613; PGS-only R2=0.02447) with similar basic covariates, but it is less phenotype-aligned (combined AF+flutter, time-to-event) and is from the same pan-trait framework family. For the second runner-up, PGS002050 is chosen over PGS001841 because both share the same combined endpoint and publication family (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”), but PGS002050 shows slightly higher partial correlation (0.1034 vs 0.1026) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with far more variants (554,908), which is structurally supportive when PRS-only AUROC/R2 are not reported for these portability models. Overall confidence is moderate because the best choice is clear on phenotype alignment and PRS-only metric availability, but the framework-study penalty and lack of disease-focused multi-cohort alternatives in the visible list limit certainty.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to autism spectrum disorder). PGS000327 is best supported because its endpoint fidelity is coherent across fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all explicitly “Autism spectrum disorder”), it comes from an ASD-focused GWAS publication context, and it provides supportive PRS-relevant evidence including an OR per SD of 1.33 (moderate) plus a reported full-model R²=0.0245 with only basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave). PGS002790 is a weaker direct match despite the ASD label because phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn),” creating endpoint ambiguity/mismatch relative to the target diagnosis; its reported partial R² (~0.0055) is also smaller and it lacks effect-size evidence. Confidence is Moderate (not High) because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUROC/R²), and the R² values shown are full/partial-model style metrics rather than explicitly PRS-only.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). The strongest support is for PGS000452 because it has high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates only (age/sex/batch/PCs), and the strongest visible performance/effect-size package among the comparable MGI-evaluated PRSweb cancer family: full-model AUROC 0.632 (CI 0.616–0.647) plus strong per-SD OR 1.663 (1.57–1.761) and top-1% vs rest OR 3.61. Runners-up PGS000454 and PGS000456 are near-clones in the same study family with essentially identical endpoint/covariates and very similar discrimination (AUROC 0.632 and 0.63, respectively) and effect sizes (per-SD OR ~1.66 and 1.63), but are slightly less supported than PGS000452 on the visible metrics. Confidence is Moderate because none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is not strictly PRS-comparable), and several models are extremely close in reported performance within the same endpoint/covariate setting, making fine ranking somewhat sensitive to non-comparable metric nuances. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait (bilirubin metabolism disease) via trait_efo/trait_reported. PGS001824 and PGS002032 have the tightest endpoint fidelity: both are explicitly "Disorders of bilirubin excretion" with trait_efo exactly "bilirubin metabolism disease" and identical covariate sets, training cohort (UKB), and reported PRS-comparable metric (partial-r=0.0716 with CI). Between these two near-clones, the visible evidence mildly favors PGS002032 structurally (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 19,768 variants vs penalized regression with 22 variants), but because both lack PRS-only AUROC/R² and report only the same partial-r, the ranking is not strongly identifiable from the provided metadata; I therefore select PGS001824 as best with only moderate confidence and keep PGS002032 as the closest runner-up. PGS000924 is a broader composite endpoint (porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism) and uses a time-to-event phenotype from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (snpnet, 5 variants), which domain guidance flags as a generalization risk despite its high reported AUROC/R²; additionally its PGS-only R² (0.218) exceeds the provided local h2_obs (~0.089), raising a sanity-check concern about metric comparability/scale, so it is ranked behind the two bilirubin-excretion-specific portability scores. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three candidates are direct matches to the target trait family (bipolar disorder) via trait_reported/trait_efo (bipolar disorder; bipolar I; bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, and similar variant counts (~935k–949k), so they form a coherent direct-match cluster. However, endpoint fidelity is unclear/possibly misaligned because phenotyping_reported fields are non-diagnostic behavioral/cognitive measures (e.g., cognitive function; DSM5 depression behavior; sluggish cognitive tempo) rather than bipolar disorder case/control status, which materially weakens direct-match support per the provided domain guidance. With no PRS-comparable AUC/PRS-only R2 and only small full_model_r2/partial R² values reported (all ~0.0025–0.0031) in modest validation samples (~2.2k–2.5k), the evidence is insufficient to clearly separate models; selection is therefore low-confidence. PGS002786 is chosen as the best-supported direct match mainly because it is the only model labeled as the umbrella trait 'Bipolar disorder' (closest concept match to the target), while PGS002787 and PGS002788 are ranked as runners-up as subtype-specific direct matches with otherwise near-identical evidence.

All three candidates are direct matches at the EFO level to the target concept (blood coagulation disease), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS002034 is preferred because it targets a clearly relevant congenital coagulation-factor deficiency endpoint and, within its same-endpoint sibling pair (PGS001826 vs PGS002034 from the same UKB portability paper with the same covariates and similar partial-r), it has the stronger structural properties (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage with 32,552 variants vs penalized regression with 45 variants) and a marginally higher reported partial correlation (0.0563 vs 0.0562). PGS001826 is the closest runner-up as the near-clone with essentially identical endpoint/covariates and nearly identical partial-r, but weaker method/variant coverage. PGS001033 is ranked third despite having explicit AUROC fields because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”) with an extremely sparse 1-variant snpnet model and a time-to-event phenotype, both of which are warning signals for generalizability per the provided domain guidance. Overall confidence is limited because the top two candidates (PGS002034/PGS001826) are from a portability framework (not disease-focused) and report only partial-r (no PRS-only AUROC/R²), while the remaining candidate’s metric evidence is discounted by its framework+sparsity+TTE design.

Direct-match candidates for breast carcinoma are abundant. Among the visible list, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) is a direct breast cancer model with endpoint-aligned phenotyping_reported (“Breast cancer”), no added covariates (“0”), and strong reported discrimination in the selected European validation (AUROC 0.6625) with accompanying PRS-comparable effect size evidence (OR 1.83, Beta 0.602). This combination (clean covariate setting + strong metrics) provides the best-supported direct-match choice from the provided candidates.

Runners-up are PGS004040 (LDpred2.CV) and PGS004025 (LDpred2-auto), which share the same endpoint (“Breast cancer”), similarly clean covariates (“0”), and nearly identical strong AUROC (~0.6598) and OR (~1.81) evidence in the same evaluation context, but are slightly weaker than PGS004153 on the reported AUROC/OR. Confidence is Moderate because many other direct-match models exist in the broader search results (179 total; 163 after filter) but only a subset is visible here, and cross-study metric comparability remains limited even when covariates appear clean.

All listed candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo and generally aligned phenotyping_reported. PGS000316 is best supported because it targets a straightforward coeliac disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Coeliac disease), is from a disease-focused clinical-care context (pilot study to aid diagnosis), and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.879 with CI 0.87–0.888) with very large validation sample size (n=379,767), making it the most evidence-rich direct-match option in the visible set. Key limitation: the reported metric is a full-model AUROC with covariates listed as Unknown, so PRS-only performance comparability is unclear.

Runner-up PGS000040 is also disease-focused with a direct coeliac disease endpoint and reports very high AUROC (0.9), but it has smaller training/validation (validation n=2,476) and similarly lacks PRS-only metrics/covariate clarity. Runner-up PGS001301 provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.82867; PGS R2 0.14224; incremental AUROC reported) and clear covariates, but it comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”) and uses a broader phenotype label (“Malabsorption/coeliac disease”), which weakens endpoint fidelity relative to the disease-focused coeliac-specific models. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; phenotyping_reported is cervical cancer/incident cervical cancer), so a direct-match exists. Among them, PGS003428 is best supported on structural grounds (LDpred genome-wide shrinkage with ~2.9M variants) and is from a cervical-phenotype GWAS meta-analysis context; it also reports an HR=1.33 (moderate per-SD effect) with basic covariates (age, smoking). Runners-up: PGS000073 has coherent endpoint fidelity (incident cervical cancer), large EUR evaluation (n=211,795), and similar basic epidemiologic covariates, but is a very sparse 10-variant GW-significant score with only modest HR=1.22 and only full-model metrics reported. PGS005165 is the best-supported non-EUR direct match (EAS GWAS/EVAL) with HR=1.20 and a moderate validation size (n=57,359), but its C-index is modest and it is also a small GWAS-hits score (15 variants). Overall confidence is limited because most reported discrimination is full-model (covariate-influenced) rather than clearly PRS-only, and several candidates are from pan-cancer/framework-style studies, making cross-model metric comparability imperfect.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis at the disease level (either exact cholelithiasis/K80 or a closely related composite of cholelithiasis+cholecystitis). The strongest direct-match support comes from the two 2024 Commun Biol models explicitly targeting ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis (PGS004546, PGS004476): they have tight endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: K80) and report per-SD effect sizes (OR), which the provided domain guidance treats as meaningful PRS-quality evidence when AUC/R2 are absent. Between these two near-clones, PGS004546 is preferred because it reports a higher OR (1.2986 vs 1.2194), a modest but direct discriminative-strength signal given otherwise similar metadata (same publication family, same variant count, same EUR-only eval, unknown covariates for both).

Runners-up: PGS004476 remains the closest alternative due to the same K80 endpoint and only slightly weaker OR evidence. For the second runner-up, PGS001174 is selected over the 2022 portability-framework scores (PGS001861/PGS002072) because it provides explicit PRS-comparable metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.623) and PGS-only R2 (0.028) plus incremental AUROC, enabling a heritability sanity check (PGS-only R2 remains below the provided h2_obs ceiling). However, it is penalized as a pan-trait UKB framework score and uses a time-to-event phenotype, which lowers confidence. Overall confidence is Moderate because the top K80 models lack AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates, while the best-metric model (PGS001174) comes from a framework study that domain guidance warns often generalizes poorly.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (CKD) via trait_efo and generally CKD-aligned phenotyping, but they vary in endpoint fidelity and how interpretable the reported performance is as PRS-specific. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD-focused with a clear clinical threshold endpoint (stage 3+; eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2), comes from a disease-focused CKD PRS paper (Nat Med: “Genome-wide polygenic score to predict chronic kidney disease across ancestries”), has large development (n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65). Although its reported AUROC (0.78) is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (so not PRS-only comparable), the endpoint fidelity plus effect-size evidence make it the most defensible direct-match choice from the visible set.

Runner-up PGS005090 is also CKD stage 3+ and CKD-focused, with strong reported full-model metrics in an African American/Afro-Caribbean evaluation (AUROC=0.9; R²=0.1) and OR=1.41, but the PRS-only contribution is unclear (full-model metrics) and it is single-ancestry (AFR-only GWAS/EVAL), making it less generally supported than PGS002237 given the context.

Runner-up PGS005113 is a direct CKD model with a strong per-SD OR=1.35 (tight CI) and CKDGen training cohort noted, but it lacks PRS-comparable metrics and has less explicit disease-focused validation framing than PGS002237.

Main limitation lowering confidence from High to Moderate: across the pool, most candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often with covariates) or only effect sizes, with limited PRS-only AUC/R² reporting; this makes cross-model performance comparability imperfect even among direct CKD endpoints.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). PGS001783 is best supported because it is a direct COPD endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both COPD), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant count (884,139), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.038092) plus an AUROC value (0.74, though not explicitly PGS-only). The R2 is also consistent with the provided heritability ceiling guidance (does not exceed the cited h2_liability ~0.0388), supporting metric plausibility. Runners-up: PGS004536 and PGS004466 are also direct COPD (ICD J44) endpoints and provide effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.49 and 1.31 respectively), but they lack explicit PRS-only AUC/R2 and have unknown covariates, reducing comparability and confidence versus PGS001783. Main limitation: several other direct-match models exist (e.g., PGS001788 with much larger validation n but lower R2; multiple snpnet UKB framework scores with explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), and the evidence does not include multi-ancestry external validation metrics for the top choice; thus confidence is moderate rather than high.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (cirrhosis of liver) via trait_efo/trait_reported, but several are alcohol-specific subtypes (PGS000704, PGS001777, PGS004913) and one has phenotype wording that appears inconsistent with its alcohol-related label (PGS000776 phenotyping_reported references NAFLD-risk individuals). PGS004621 is best supported as a general cirrhosis PRS: it matches the target EFO exactly (cirrhosis of liver), has endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported ('Cirrhosis'), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large variant count (1,089,806), and comes from a disease-focused Nat Genet study with large multi-cohort development and very large validation (n=1,153,995). However, confidence is limited because the only discrimination metric shown is a full-model AUROC (0.68) rather than an explicitly PRS-only metric, making cross-model performance comparability weaker per the provided domain guidance.
